rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.3, field experiment March 2018-July 2019 in a solar greenhouse in Tianjin, four treatments x three replicates, split-plot design, measuring N2O fluxes, N leaching and tomato yield over three seasons. Q2: Section 3.1 and Fig. 1a: annual tomato yield about 147 t/ha for CIF and in tendency ~10% higher for DIF treatments, straw incorporation did not affect yield; Section 3.2/Table 1/Fig. 1d: annual N2O emissions 9.6-9.9 kg N/ha in DIF/DIFS vs 47.8-78.5 in CIF/CIFS; Section 3.3/Table 2: annual NO3 leaching 67-89 kg N/ha for DIF/DIFS vs 603-788 for CIF/CIFS; Discussion opening: drip fertigation with straw reduces N2O by 80% and N leaching by 88% versus flooding fertigation. Q4: Section 2.3 and 3.4/Fig. S2: hourly soil WFPS and temperature (TDR) and topsoil mineral N measured; N2O and NO3 leaching showed significant positive correlations with WFPS, temperature and mineral N; Fig. 5 reports plant N uptake as 45-48% of input for DIFs vs 15-16% for CIFs. Q8: Section 4.2 states the study does not answer whether applied irrigation and fertilisation rates are optimal, which would need modelling and true replicated multifactorial experiments the authors could not realise (also Conclusions); Section 4.2 notes the low DON leaching for CIF may be a legacy effect of suction-cup installation creating preferential flow pathways. Q9: Fig. 1 reports annual means <U+00B1> SE (N=9) for yield, N2O and WUE; Tables 1 and 2 give seasonal and annual N2O and leaching values <U+00B1> SE.
rows.notes: Q3 no: N2O by static chambers only, leaching by suction cups plus tensiometer flux only, yield by harvest weighing; no independent second method for any of the claimed effects. Q5/Q6 no: single site, single crop (tomato cultivar Chaoyanshengdi), plot scale (6.7 x 3.6 m). Q7 doubtful: Discussion attributes the drip effect to low-amount high-frequency fertigation matched to plant demand and the reduced N rate (41% of CIF), and attributes absence of straw-induced N2O increase under DIF to low soil N availability, but these are offered as explanations/attributions rather than stated requirements, so rated no. Note the claim says 'minimized'; study shows strong reductions relative to CIF but authors say rates may not be optimal.

notes: Full text available; supplementary tables/figures (S1, S2, Table S1, S2) referenced but not included. Treatment is drip fertigation with reduced N fertilisation (not drip alone), so the reductions reflect combined irrigation and fertiliser changes versus flooding with over-fertilisation.
